     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0Functor
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
    10	
    11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
    12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
    13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
    14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
    15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
    16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
    17	
    18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
    19	
    20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
    21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
    22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
    23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
    24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
    25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
    26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
    27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
    28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
    29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
    30	
    31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
    32	
    33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
    35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
    36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
    37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
    38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
    39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
    40	
    41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
    42	
    43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
    44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
    45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
    46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
    47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
    48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
    49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
    50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
    51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
    52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
    53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
    54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
    55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
    61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
    63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
    65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
    66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
    67	-/
    68	
    69	set_option autoImplicit false
    70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    71	
    72	universe u
    73	
    74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    75	
    76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    77	
    78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    79	
    80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
    82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
    83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
    84	
    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
   101	
   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData
   147	
   148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
   149	registered)
   150	
   151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
   152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
   153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
   154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
   155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
   156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
   157	
   158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   159	
   160	open MonObj
   161	
   162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   164	
   165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
   166	elaborates with no transport. -/
   167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   168	
   169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
   170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
   171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
   172	defeq). -/
   173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
   174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
   177	
   178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
   179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
   180	scope). -/
   181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
   182	  inferInstance
   183	
   184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   185	
   186	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-- **CUSTOM.** The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with
    66	morphisms the morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc
    83	
    84	-- data
    85	/-- **ADAPTED.** The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
    89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
    93	
    94	-- data
    95	/-- **ADAPTED.** The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
    96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    99	  sorry
   100	
   101	namespace Jacobian
   102	
   103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
   104	
   105	-- data
   106	/-- **ADAPTED.** The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
   107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
   108	  sorry
   109	
   110	/-- **ADAPTED.** The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
   111	genus of `C`. -/
   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
   113	  sorry
   114	
   115	/-- **ADAPTED.**
   116	
   117	**TO CHECK:** The blueprint's named Lean target is unresolved because this instance is declared
   118	anonymously. The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
   119	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
   120	  sorry
   121	
   122	/-- **ADAPTED.**
   123	
   124	**TO CHECK:** The blueprint's named Lean target is unresolved because this instance is declared
   125	anonymously. The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   126	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   127	  sorry
   128	
   129	/-- **ADAPTED.** The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
   130	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
   131	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
   132	  sorry
   133	
   134	/-- **ADAPTED.** The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0`
   135	(denoted by `η`) is the neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
   136	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   137	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   138	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   139	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
   140	  sorry
   141	
   142	/--
   143	**ADAPTED.**
   144	
   145	**TO CHECK:** Milne's Proposition 6.1 assumes positive genus, while this declaration also covers
   146	genus zero (`references/abelian-varieties/tex/page-0110.tex`).
   147	
   148	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
   149	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
   150	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
   151	-/
   152	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   153	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   154	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   155	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
   156	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   157	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
   158	  sorry
   159	
   160	/-- **CUSTOM.** **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a
   161	curve goes to its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line
   162	bundles. The functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action
   163	is pinned to the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of
   164	`Jacobian C`. -/
   165	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   166	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
   167	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
   168	  map _ := sorry
   169	  map_id := sorry
   170	  map_comp := sorry

   174	/-! ## Base change of fields
   175	
   176	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   177	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
   178	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
   179	
   180	/-- **CUSTOM.** Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e.
   181	`X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. -/
   182	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   183	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   184	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   185	
   186	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   187	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   188	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   189	
   190	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   191	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   192	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   193	
   194	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   195	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
   196	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   197	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
   198	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
   199	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   200	
   201	-- The coherences mention curves of the form `(𝟭 _).obj C` and `(F ⋙ G).obj C`.
   202	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
   203	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   204	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   205	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   206	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
   207	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   208	
   209	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
   210	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
   211	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   212	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
   213	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
   214	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   215	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   216	  inferInstanceAs (GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
   217	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
   218	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
   219	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   220	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
   221	
   222	/-- Base change along `k → k` is the identity functor. -/
   223	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   224	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
   225	  eqToIso (by
   226	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
   227	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
   228	
   229	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
   230	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   231	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
   232	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
   233	  eqToIso (by
   234	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
   235	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
   236	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   237	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
   238	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
   239	
   240	namespace Jacobian
   241	
   242	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
   243	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
   244	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
   245	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   246	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   247	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
   248	    (e : C ≅ C') :
   249	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
   250	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
   251	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
   252	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
   253	
   254	/-- **CUSTOM.** **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a
   255	canonical isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
   256	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   257	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   258	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   259	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
   260	  sorry
   261	
   262	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
   263	
   264	/-- **CUSTOM.** Identity coherence. -/
   265	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   266	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   267	    baseChangeIso k k C =
   268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
   269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
   270	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
   271	  sorry
   272	
   273	/-- **CUSTOM.** Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
   274	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   275	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
   276	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   277	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   278	    baseChangeIso k M C
   279	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
   280	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
   281	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
   282	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
   283	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   284	  sorry
   285	
   286	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
   287	
   288	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   289	
   290	/-- **CUSTOM.** -/
   291	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   292	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   293	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   294	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
   295	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
   296	  sorry
   297	
   298	end Jacobian

    13	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
    14	
    15	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
    16	its structure as an abelian variety.
    17	
    18	## Status
    19	
    20	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
    21	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
    22	project from the witness directly.
    23	
    24	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
    25	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
    26	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
    27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
    28	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
    29	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
    30	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
    31	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
    32	
    33	`picardJacobianWitness` is wired to the `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development in its **étale** form
    34	(`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`): the witness scheme is `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C`, the identity
    35	component of the scheme representing the *étale-sheafified* relative Picard functor. It
    36	carries **no hypothesis on `C(k)`** — exactly the three challenge hypotheses and nothing
    37	else — which is the owner decision of 2026-07-28 (protection I-0491) and the full strength
    38	the challenge asks for.
    39	
    40	Why sheafifying is what makes that possible. Over an arbitrary field one cannot ask for
    41	representability of the *unsheafified* functor `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    42	(`picSharp`): Kleiman L5105–L5108 exhibits the conic `u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — a
    43	smooth plane conic, hence smooth, proper and geometrically integral, over a field where it
    44	has no rational point — for which he concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable while
    45	`Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is. The étale sheafification is Kleiman's own object; its sheaf property is
    46	*proved* in `Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`picEt_isSheaf_forget`), not assumed.
    47	
    48	**Two corrections to what this paragraph used to say** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30), both of
    49	which had already been made at the seam and in the blueprint and were missed *here*, in the
    50	file a reader opens first.
    51	
    52	*The reason was wrong.* This said `picSharp` "is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally". No
    53	source supports that for the **relative** functor: the lines it came from
    54	(Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302) are about the **absolute** `Pic_X`, and `picSharp` is *defined* by
    55	quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. Kleiman's own claim about the
    56	relative functor is the much weaker "not *a priori* a sheaf" (L1330), and `th:cmp` part 1
    57	points the other way — `Pic_{X/S}` *injects* into `Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever
    58	`O_S = f_*O_X` universally, automatic on these binders, so **in Kleiman** `picSharp` is
    59	Zariski-*separated* here.
    60	
    61	That last sentence is a statement about the SOURCE, and the Lean citation I first attached
    62	to it does not carry it (`review-ajc`, corrected in the same session by a fresh-context
    63	audit of my own fix). `PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`
    64	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) takes a `rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X`
    65	hypothesis: it says a *representable* `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf, by subcanonicity —
    66	which is the converse direction and is conditional on the thing the seam does not have.
    67	`PicEtSubcanonical`'s own §4 docstring scopes it correctly as "only the first half"; that
    68	caveat is what I dropped when I copied the citation here. Nothing in this project proves
    69	`th:cmp` part 1. Do not restore a Zariski-sheaf reason in this slot; two replacement
    70	citations have already been wrong in it (`I-0970`, `I-0973`), and this was a third.
    71	
    72	*And "**false**" overstates what is proved.* The non-representability of `picSharp` is a
    73	Lean theorem only *conditionally*:
    74	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
    75	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) derives from `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` that no scheme
    76	represents `picSharp C`. Its antecedent — that the comparison genuinely fails for that conic
    77	— is **quoted from Kleiman, not formalised here**; doing so means exhibiting `φ^*O(1)` in
    78	`picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image via `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`. So the accurate word for the
    79	unsheafified statement over arbitrary `k` is **unproved with a refutation route mapped
    80	out**, not "false". `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` says exactly this at
    81	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, and says that writing "FALSE" here is the error the board row
    82	was corrected for in the opposite direction.
    83	
    84	## The five obligations, and none of them is false
    85	
    86	Be precise about what the wiring buys, because "invoked upstream" is not "proved
    87	upstream". The witness reaches **five** open obligations:
    88	
    89	1. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` — representability of the étale-sheafified functor
    90	   over an arbitrary field (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). The project's central
    91	   open obligation, expected to stay open;
    92	2. `Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` — Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero, a
    93	   genuine statement in characteristic `p`;
    94	3. `Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed` — Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`;
    95	4. `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`, 5. `isAlbanese_pic0Et` — the two leaves
    96	   stated below, each at exactly the strength the assembly consumes.
    97	
    98	Note (2) and (3) rather than smoothness and properness: `Pic0Et.smooth` and
    99	`Pic0Et.proper` are **assemblies** over them, not obligations of their own, and citing
   100	them as the open statements is a stale reading. What *is* proved unconditionally, and
   101	measures axiom-clean: `Pic0Et.grpObj`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible`,
   102	`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0Et.isSeparated`.
   103	
   104	**The five are NOT independent, and the list must not be read as five distances to be
   105	added** — measured 2026-07-29 r2 (`ajc-p2`, `Picard/Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean`;
   106	independently reproduced by `ajc-p3`). Obligation 4 **implies** obligation 2: leaf B gives
   107	bare smoothness by `SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth` and then geometric reducedness by
   108	this project's `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, packaged as
   109	`Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced_of_leafB`. So closing leaf B would close two of the
   110	five at once, and obligation 2 is a *sub-problem* of obligation 4 rather than a peer of
   111	it. What does **not** follow is that obligation 2 became cheaper: it is the weaker
   112	statement, so proving it directly (the `k̄` reduction on `AJC.pic0av.structure`) remains
   113	the right attack, and the implication is useless in that direction. The other three are
   114	mutually independent as far as anything measured shows.
   115	
   116	**All five are true statements awaiting proofs**, and that is the substance of the 2026-07-28
   117	change rather than the count. The former leaf `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` asserted a
   118	`k`-rational point from the challenge hypotheses alone; it was *false*, so the witness rested
   119	on an inconsistent hypothesis and its consequences were vacuously true — a state no axiom
   120	check can distinguish from an honest one. It has been deleted, never proved. The count was
   121	five before and is five now; what changed is that no obligation is a false statement any
   122	more.
   123	
   124	That the headline carries no rational-point binder is **checked**, not asserted: the
   125	`HeadlineBinders` section of `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` elaborates every headline
   126	declaration under exactly the three challenge hypotheses and stops compiling if a
   127	`[HasRationalPoint _]` binder ever returns.
   128	
   129	Two conditional results are kept beside the headline and **neither may be presented as
   130	it**: `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, the same assembly on the *unsheafified*
   131	functor with `C(k) ≠ ∅` as a hypothesis (true, strictly weaker than the challenge), and
   132	`picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`, a genuine theorem over `k̄`. Their gate
   133	`Scheme.HasPicScheme` has no instance: its only producer is the named theorem
   134	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so nothing acquires a rational point by synthesis.
   135	
   136	The two étale leaves are each stated at exactly the strength the assembly consumes, and
   137	each carries a *companion* measuring what the landed development already reaches, so the
   138	remaining distance is compiler-checked rather than described:
   139	
   140	- `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` refined to
   141	  relative dimension `genus C`. `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus` measures what remains:
   142	  the leaf owes a translation between two invariants of smoothness — the tangent-space
   143	  dimension and the rank of `Ω`, which is what Mathlib's presentation-based
   144	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` is characterised by. Two corrections to what this entry used
   145	  to say, both from the 2026-07-29 pass (`ajc-p2`, `I-0975`): the dimension count is *not*
   146	  "landed mathematics" — `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` reports
   147	  `sorryAx`; and there is no "transport of that landed chain from `Pic0Scheme` to
   148	  `Pic0SchemeEt`" to pay for, because the chain **restates** at the étale object with no
   149	  comparison of the two Picard schemes (`Picard/Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean`). The étale
   150	  formulation's own dimension count is proved there from a single named antecedent.
   151	- `isAlbanese_pic0Et` — the Albanese universal property over an arbitrary base field and
   152	  for every marked point, where the landed proof covers the algebraically closed,
   153	  positive-genus case. `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` measures the distance exactly:
   154	  in that case the universal property *is* the landed
   155	  `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` with no transport, and what the leaf adds
   156	  is arbitrary base field, genus `0`, and the basepoint condition `P ≫ ι_P = η`.
   157	
   158	The `picSharp`-shaped leaves `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` and `isAlbanese_pic0`
   159	are retained below: they are the obligations of the *conditional* milestone
   160	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, not of the headline.
   161	
   162	The file contains:
   163	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
   164	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
   165	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
   166	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
   167	- `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`: the Picard development's `GeometricallyIntegral`
   168	  hypothesis, derived from the challenge hypotheses.
   169	- `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus` and `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`: the parts of
   170	  leaves B and C that the landed development already proves, stated at the headline so
   171	  that each leaf's remaining distance is compiler-checked rather than described.
   172	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed` and `picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`:
   173	  leaf A discharged over an algebraically closed field, and the witness assembled without
   174	  the inconsistent leaf. Unlike the two companions above the first of these is axiom-clean
   175	  and is a discharge rather than a record of distance.
   176	- `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`: the assembly itself, with the rational point
   177	  as a hypothesis rather than a source. Both witnesses below are `haveI` specialisations of
   178	  it, so neither repeats a field, and it is the compiled form of branch (1) of the open
   179	  decision — a headline carrying `C(k) ≠ ∅` needs no new mathematics beyond this. Branch
   180	  (2) is not reachable from it; see its docstring.
   181	- the four leaves above — two in the `picSharp` shape, two in the étale shape — and
   182	  `picardJacobianWitness`, the Albanese witness `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}` assembled from the
   183	  étale pair with no `sorry` of its own.
   184	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
   185	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
   186	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
   187	  Albanese witness.
   188	
   189	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
   190	
   191	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
   192	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
   193	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
   194	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
   195	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
   196	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
   197	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
   198	-/

   204	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
   205	
   206	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   207	
   208	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   209	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   210	  [IsProper C.hom]
   211	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   212	
   213	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
   214	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
   215	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
   216	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   217	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   218	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
   219	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
   220	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]

that extension with any ambient map which commutes with the direct scalar extension.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

namespace AlgebraicJacobian

noncomputable section

/-- Scalar extension of an algebra map.  This is the map-level form of
`scalarExtensionMap`, whose special case induced by an algebra structure is recorded
separately in the pushout base-change file. -/
def scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom {R K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    (K ⊗[R] A) →ₐ[K] (K ⊗[R] B) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id K K) f

/-- `scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom` sends a pure tensor by applying the original map to
its algebra factor. -/
@[simp]
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul {R K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (c : K) (a : A) :
    scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) f (c ⊗ₜ[R] a) =
      c ⊗ₜ[R] f a := by
  simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Scalar extension of a map is natural in a tower of scalar rings. -/
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower {F L K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    [Algebra F A] [Algebra F B]
    (f : A →ₐ[F] B) :
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
        (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
        ((scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := F) (K := L) f).restrictScalars F) =
      ((scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := F) (K := K) f).restrictScalars F).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
          (AlgHom.id F A)) := by
  ext x
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Scalar extension preserves composition of algebra maps. -/
@[simp]
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_comp {R K A B D : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B] [Semiring D]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R D]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : B →ₐ[R] D) :
    (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) g).comp
        (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) f) =
      scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) (g.comp f) := by
  ext x
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Scalar extension preserves the identity algebra map. -/
@[simp]
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_id {R K A : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] :
    scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) (AlgHom.id R A) =
      AlgHom.id K (K ⊗[R] A) := by
  ext x
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Cancellation on a tensor whose right factor is itself a scalar extension. -/
theorem cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange {F L K A : Type u}
    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    [Algebra F A] (c : K) (x : L ⊗[F] A) :
    Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A (c ⊗ₜ[L] x) =
      c • Algebra.TensorProduct.map
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A) x := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
  | zero => simp
  | add x y hx hy =>
      rw [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy, map_add, smul_add]
  | tmul l a =>
      simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange_tmul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]

/-- Cancellation is natural for maps between two base changes from `F` to `L` which
commute with their direct scalar extensions from `L` to `K`. -/
theorem cancelBaseChange_naturality {F L K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    [Algebra F A] [Algebra F B]
    (phiL : L ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[F] B)
    (phiK : K ⊗[F] A →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] B)
    (hphi :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
          (phiL.restrictScalars F) =
        (phiK.restrictScalars F).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A))) :
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K B).toAlgHom.comp
        (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := L) (K := K) phiL) =
      phiK.comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A).toAlgHom := by
  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
  intro x
  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
  | zero => simp
  | add x y hx hy => simp [map_add, hx, hy]
  | tmul c x =>
      change Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K B
          (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := L) (K := K) phiL (c ⊗ₜ[L] x)) =
        phiK (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A (c ⊗ₜ[L] x))
      rw [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul, cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange,
        cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange]
      rw [show phiK (c • (Algebra.TensorProduct.map
          (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A)) x) =
          c • phiK ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map
            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A)) x) from
        phiK.toLinearMap.map_smul c _]
      have h := DFunLike.congr_fun hphi x
      change
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F B))
            (phiL x) =
          phiK ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
            (AlgHom.id F A)) x) at h
      exact congrArg (fun z => c • z) h

end

            (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceRight

          (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.TensorFiniteSubextension

/-!
# Algebra maps at finite subextensions

An algebra map between scalar extensions from `F` to an algebraic field extension `K`
is already defined over a finite subextension when its source algebra is of finite type.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0

/-- A `K`-algebra map between base changes of `F`-algebras descends to a finite
subextension of `K/F` when the source algebra is of finite type. The descended map
commutes with the canonical maps to the original `K`-algebras. -/
theorem exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_algHom
    {F K A B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K] [CommRing A] [Algebra F A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType F A] [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
    (phi : K ⊗[F] A →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] B) :
    ∃ L : FinSubext F K, ∃ phiL : L.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] B,
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
          (phiL.restrictScalars F) =
        (phi.restrictScalars F).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)) := by
  let fA : A →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B :=
    (phi.restrictScalars F).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
  have hfA : fA.range.FG := by
    simpa only [Algebra.map_top] using
      (Subalgebra.FG.map fA Algebra.FiniteType.out)
  obtain ⟨L, g, hg⟩ :=
    exists_finSubext_fg_subalgebra_tensorProduct_factor fA.range hfA
  let fL : A →ₐ[F] L.1 ⊗[F] B := g.comp fA.rangeRestrict
  let phiL : L.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] B :=
    AlgHom.liftEquiv F L.1 A (L.1 ⊗[F] B) fL
  have hbase (a : A) :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)) (fL a) = fA a := by
    change ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp g)
      (fA.rangeRestrict a) = fA a
    rw [hg]
    rfl
  refine ⟨L, phiL, ?_⟩
  ext x
  · change (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B))
        (phiL (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := F) (S := L.1)
          (A := L.1) (B := A) x)) =
      phi ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A))
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := F) (S := L.1)
          (A := L.1) (B := A) x))
    simp only [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft_apply, phiL, AlgHom.liftEquiv_tmul,
      Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, map_one]
    simpa [Algebra.smul_def] using (phi.commutes (x : K)).symm
  · change (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B))
        (phiL (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := F) (A := L.1) (B := A) x)) =
      phi ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A))
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := F) (A := L.1) (B := A) x))
    simp only [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply, phiL, AlgHom.liftEquiv_tmul,
      Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.id_apply, map_one, one_smul]
    exact hbase x

/-- Two algebra maps at a finite tensor stage are equal if their composites with the
canonical map to the ambient algebraic extension are equal.  This is the equation-reflection
step used after spreading inverse and cocycle identities. -/
theorem tensorProduct_algHom_eq_of_map_comp_eq
    {F K A B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K] [CommRing A] [Algebra F A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] (L : FinSubext F K)
    (phi psi : L.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] B)
    (h :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
          (phi.restrictScalars F) =
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
          (psi.restrictScalars F)) :
    phi = psi := by
  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
  intro x
  apply tensorProduct_map_finSubext_injective L
  exact congrArg (fun f => f x) h

/-- A composition identity descends once all three maps commute with base change.  This is
the equation step needed after spreading transition maps: inverse and cocycle identities can
be checked over the ambient algebraic extension and then reflected to the finite stage. -/
theorem tensorProduct_algHom_comp_eq_of_baseChange
    {F K A B D : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
    [CommRing D] [Algebra F D] (L : FinSubext F K)
    (phiL : L.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] B)
    (psiL : L.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] D)
    (chiL : L.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] D)
    (phiK : K ⊗[F] A →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] B)
    (psiK : K ⊗[F] B →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] D)
    (chiK : K ⊗[F] A →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] D)
    (hphi :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
          (phiL.restrictScalars F) =
        (phiK.restrictScalars F).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)))
    (hpsi :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F D)).comp
          (psiL.restrictScalars F) =
        (psiK.restrictScalars F).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)))
    (hchi :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F D)).comp
          (chiL.restrictScalars F) =
        (chiK.restrictScalars F).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)))
    (hK : psiK.comp phiK = chiK) :
    psiL.comp phiL = chiL := by
  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
  intro x
  apply tensorProduct_map_finSubext_injective L
  calc
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F D))
        ((psiL.comp phiL) x) =
      psiK ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)) (phiL x)) := by
        exact DFunLike.congr_fun hpsi (phiL x)
    _ = psiK (phiK
        ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)) x)) := by
      exact congrArg psiK (DFunLike.congr_fun hphi x)
    _ = chiK ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)) x) := by
      exact DFunLike.congr_fun hK
        ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)) x)
    _ = (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F D)) (chiL x) := by
      exact (DFunLike.congr_fun hchi x).symm

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
-- The dependent finite family creates one tensor-product algebra instance per member.
/-- A finite family of algebra maps between base changes of `F`-algebras descends to one
common finite subextension of `K/F` when every source algebra is of finite type. -/
theorem exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_algHom_finite
    {F K : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (A B : ι → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra F (A i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra.FiniteType F (A i)]
    [∀ i, CommRing (B i)] [∀ i, Algebra F (B i)]
    (phi : ∀ i, K ⊗[F] A i →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] B i) :
    ∃ L : FinSubext F K, ∀ i,
      ∃ phiL : L.1 ⊗[F] A i →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] B i,
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (B i))).comp
            (phiL.restrictScalars F) =
          ((phi i).restrictScalars F).comp
            (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (A i))) := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  choose Li phiLi hphiLi using fun i =>
    exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_algHom (phi i)
  let A0i (i : ι) : Subalgebra F K := (Li i).1.toSubalgebra
  have hA0i (i : ι) : (A0i i).FG := by
    rw [Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType]
    change Algebra.FiniteType F (Li i).1
    infer_instance
  let A0 : Subalgebra F K := Finset.univ.sup A0i
  have hA0 : A0.FG := by
    dsimp only [A0]
    induction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => simpa using (Subalgebra.fg_bot : (⊥ : Subalgebra F K).FG)
    | @insert i s hi hs =>
        simpa [Finset.sup_insert] using (hA0i i).sup hs
  have hA0iA0 : ∀ i, A0i i ≤ A0 := fun i =>
    Finset.le_sup (s := Finset.univ) (f := A0i) (Finset.mem_univ i)
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F A0 :=
    Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_injective A0.val Subtype.val_injective
  let L0 : IntermediateField F K := Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField A0
  letI : Algebra.FiniteType F L0 := by
    change Algebra.FiniteType F A0
    exact (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType A0).mp hA0
  letI : Module.Finite F L0 := Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic
  let L : FinSubext F K := ⟨L0, inferInstance⟩
  refine ⟨L, ?_⟩
  intro i
  have hLiL : (Li i).1 ≤ L.1 := hA0iA0 i
  let inc : (Li i).1 →ₐ[F] L.1 := IntermediateField.inclusion hLiL
  let fL : A i →ₐ[F] L.1 ⊗[F] B i :=
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map inc (AlgHom.id F (B i))).comp
      ((phiLi i).restrictScalars F |>.comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := F) (A := (Li i).1) (B := A i)))
  let phiL : L.1 ⊗[F] A i →ₐ[L.1] L.1 ⊗[F] B i :=
    AlgHom.liftEquiv F L.1 (A i) (L.1 ⊗[F] B i) fL
  have hmap :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (B i))).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map inc (AlgHom.id F (B i))) =
        Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Li i).1.val (AlgHom.id F (B i)) := by
    ext x <;> rfl
  refine ⟨phiL, ?_⟩
  ext x
  · change (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (B i)))
        (phiL (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := F) (S := L.1)
          (A := L.1) (B := A i) x)) =
      phi i ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (A i)))
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := F) (S := L.1)
          (A := L.1) (B := A i) x))
    simp only [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft_apply, phiL, AlgHom.liftEquiv_tmul,
      Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, map_one]
    simpa [Algebra.smul_def] using ((phi i).commutes (x : K)).symm
  · change (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (B i)))
        (phiL (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := F) (A := L.1) (B := A i) x)) =
      phi i ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F (A i)))
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := F) (A := L.1) (B := A i) x))
    simp only [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply, phiL, AlgHom.liftEquiv_tmul,
      Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.id_apply, map_one, one_smul, fL,
      AlgHom.comp_apply]
    rw [← AlgHom.comp_apply, hmap]
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun (hphiLi i)
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := F) (A := (Li i).1) (B := A i) x)

+# Reflection of the finite-stage triple-transition face equation
+
+The canonical maps out of tensor products carry dependent module and algebra instances.
+This file keeps those instances coherent by packaging a finite-stage transition, the two
+canonical comparison maps, and their square under one inference boundary.  Applying the
+package to the two paths around a triple-overlap face reflects the ambient face equation
+without rebuilding any tensor-product carrier metadata.

+

+/-- A scalar-extension face diagram together with the canonical comparison square for its
+lower transition.  All four algebra carriers and their instances are parameters of one
+structure, so projections never resynthesize tensor-product metadata. -/
+structure ScalarExtensionFacePackage
+    {F K A B D E : Type u}
+    [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
+    [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
+    [CommRing D] [Algebra F D] [CommRing E] [Algebra F E]
+    (N : DatG0.FinSubext F K) where
+  thetaN : N.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[N.1] N.1 ⊗[F] E
+  tauN : N.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[N.1] N.1 ⊗[F] D
+  rightN : N.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[N.1] N.1 ⊗[F] B
+  leftN : N.1 ⊗[F] D →ₐ[N.1] N.1 ⊗[F] E
+  sourceComparison : N.1 ⊗[F] A →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] A
+  targetComparison : N.1 ⊗[F] D →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] D
+  tau_square :
+    targetComparison.comp (tauN.restrictScalars F) =
+      (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+        (R := F) (K := K) (AlgHom.id F D)).comp sourceComparison
+  face : thetaN.comp rightN = leftN.comp tauN
+
+/-- Package a commutative scalar-extension face diagram.  The result type is inferred from
+the four maps, forcing every occurrence of the intermediate carriers to retain the same
+ring and algebra instances. -/
+noncomputable def scalarExtensionFacePackage
+    {F K A B D E : Type u}
+    [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
+    [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
+    [CommRing D] [Algebra F D] [CommRing E] [Algebra F E]
+    (N : DatG0.FinSubext F K)
+    (right : A →ₐ[F] B) (tau : A →ₐ[F] D) (left : D →ₐ[F] E)
+    (thetaN : N.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[N.1] N.1 ⊗[F] E)
+    (thetaK : K ⊗[F] B →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] E)
+    (htheta :
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F E)).comp
+          (thetaN.restrictScalars F) =
+        (thetaK.restrictScalars F).comp
+          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)))
+    (hfaceK :
+      thetaK.comp
+          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) right) =
+        (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+          (R := F) (K := K) left).comp
+          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) tau)) := by
+  let rightN := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+    (R := F) (K := N.1) right
+  let tauN := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+    (R := F) (K := N.1) tau
+  let leftN := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+    (R := F) (K := N.1) left
+  let sourceComparison :=
+    Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)
+  let middleComparison :=
+    Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)
+  let targetComparison :=
+    Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F D)
+  let faceTargetComparison :=
+    Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F E)
+  have hval : N.1.val = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F N.1 K := by
+    ext x
+    rfl
+  have hright := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower
+    (F := F) (L := N.1) (K := K) right
+  have htau := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower
+    (F := F) (L := N.1) (K := K) tau
+  have hleft := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower
+    (F := F) (L := N.1) (K := K) left
+  rw [← hval] at hright htau hleft
+  have hcomposite :
+      faceTargetComparison.comp ((leftN.comp tauN).restrictScalars F) =
+        (((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+          (R := F) (K := K) left).comp
+            (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+              (R := F) (K := K) tau)).restrictScalars F).comp
+          sourceComparison := by
+    apply DFunLike.ext _ _
+    intro x
+    calc
+      faceTargetComparison ((leftN.comp tauN) x) =
+          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) left) (targetComparison (tauN x)) :=
+        DFunLike.congr_fun hleft (tauN x)
+      _ = (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) left)
+          ((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) tau) (sourceComparison x)) := by
+        exact congrArg
+          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) left)
+          (DFunLike.congr_fun htau x)
+      _ = (((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+            (R := F) (K := K) left).comp
+              (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+                (R := F) (K := K) tau)).restrictScalars F).comp
+            sourceComparison x := rfl
+  have hface : thetaN.comp rightN = leftN.comp tauN := by
+    apply DatG0.tensorProduct_algHom_comp_eq_of_baseChange N
+      rightN thetaN (leftN.comp tauN)
+      (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+        (R := F) (K := K) right)
+      thetaK
+      ((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+        (R := F) (K := K) left).comp
+        (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
+          (R := F) (K := K) tau))
+    · exact hright
+    · exact htheta
+    · exact hcomposite
+    · exact hfaceK

+    tauN := tauN
+    rightN := rightN
+    leftN := leftN
+    sourceComparison := sourceComparison
+    targetComparison := targetComparison
+    tau_square := htau

+variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
+  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]

+section

+variable {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
+variable (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
+variable (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C → Nat)
+variable (relation : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
+variable (e : ∀ j,

+    Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
+variable (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
+variable [Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k]
+variable (mapM : ∀ q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
+  Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
+      (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
+    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M

+variable (hmapM : ∀ q,
+  (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
+      (AlgHom.id L.1
+        (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
+          (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
+          (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
+          (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
+      ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
+    ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
+      L.1).comp
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
+        (AlgHom.id L.1
+          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
+            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
+            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
+            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))))))
+
+/-- The inferred package for one Picard triple-transition face. -/
+noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionFacePackage
+    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
+    (U V W : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C)
+    (thetaN : ∀ p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
+      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
+          C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
+        N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
+          C L n m relation M mapM p)
+    (hthetaN : ∀ p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
+          (AlgHom.id M.1
+            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
+              C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
+          ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
+        ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
+          C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
+            M.1).comp
+          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
+            (AlgHom.id M.1
+              (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
+                C L n m relation M mapM p)))) :=
+  scalarExtensionFacePackage N
+    (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceRight
+      C L n m relation M mapM V W U)
+    (mapM (Sum.inr (U, V)))
+    (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
+      C L n m relation M mapM U V W)
+    (thetaN (U, (V, W)))
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
+      C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM U V W)
+    (hthetaN (U, (V, W)))
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransition_fac
+      C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM U V W)
+
+/-- The ambient triple-transition face equation reflects to the common finite stage `N`.
+The statement uses the inferred package projections so its tensor-product instances are
+definitionally identical to those used to construct the descended maps. -/
+theorem pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModel_fac
+    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
+    (U V W : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C)
+    (thetaN : ∀ p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
+      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
+          C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
+        N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
+          C L n m relation M mapM p)
+    (hthetaN : ∀ p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
+          (AlgHom.id M.1
+            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
+              C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
+          ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
+        ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
+          C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
+            M.1).comp
+          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
+            (AlgHom.id M.1
+              (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
+                C L n m relation M mapM p)))) :
+    let P := pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionFacePackage
+      C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM N U V W thetaN hthetaN
+    P.thetaN.comp P.rightN = P.leftN.comp P.tauN := by
+  exact (pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionFacePackage
+    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM N U V W thetaN hthetaN).face
+
+end
+
+end
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry
